title: NovusAI - embeddings + rerank discovery
meeting_header: Date: 2026-02-25 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Host: Sofia Park (Redwood AE) | Recording: enabled
summary: Discovery call to understand NovusAI's current embeddings/reranking pipeline, vector DB integration, throughput and latency targets, and security requirements to propose Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Strong interest in hybrid search (keywords + vector), high QPS (5k-20k), and SOC2/KMS requirements.
transcript: [00:00] Sofia (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining — i'm sofia from redwood, and with me is ethan our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Priya (Head of ML): good thanks, priya here. excited to dig in, we've been evaluating vector options for the last quarter.
[00:12] Daniel (CTO): yeah i'll jump in where needed. we run a customer-facing search product — about ~50M docs currently.
[00:18] Ethan (SE): awesome. so high-level — are you mostly interested in embeddings-only or embedding + rerank hybrid flow?
[00:25] Priya: hybrid — we do a keyword-first filter then embed rerank. we experimented with faiss on-proc but the ops cost is high. latency is a big factor, tail p95 under 300ms ideally.
[00:34] Sofia: that's helpful. when you say ops cost high, is that CPU/GPU infra or engineering maintenance?
[00:39] Priya: both. faiss on cloud requires a bunch of tuning, sharding; we saw throughput drop with long tails when cold caches. also we want simpler autoscale for peak traffic.
[00:48] Maya (SRE): plus we have multi-region constraints; some traffic from EU requires data residency. security is big — SOC2 is required, KMS or HSM for key management ideally.
[00:57] Ethan: makes sense. quick question: what embedding dimensionality are you currently using? 768, 1536?
[01:02] Priya: 1536 from the model we use today — small proprietary model. thinking about switching to open 1.5k models or trying 768 for cost savings but worried about quality.

[01:10] Sofia: yeah that's a typical tradeoff. on redwood we can serve embeddings from hosted models or you can bring your model to dedicated/private. we also provide verified performance profiles for common embedding dims.
[01:18] Daniel: curious about vector DB integration — we use Postgres for metadata and currently talk to milvus for indexing. how would redwood fit that?

[01:24] Ethan: there are two patterns we see: 1) redwood-hosted for embeddings API + external vector DB (milvus/pinecone/your faiss layer) where you push vectors as normal, or 2) use redwood dedicated/private and co-locate the index with the runtime for lower latency and higher throughput. both supported.
[01:36] Priya: co-locating sounds appealing. for our peak we need ~10k qps of embedding lookups for initial filter — is that realistic?

[01:42] Ethan: the split matters — 10k lookup qps for ANN probe is different than 10k full re-ranks. if you do sparse pre-filtering and only rerank top 100 candidates with a reranker model, dedicated setups can hit that with batching and sharded indices. hosted can as well but we'd likely recommend dedicated for predictable throughput.
[01:57] Maya: what about hybrid search? we want to do BM25 + vector, and weight them. any built-in support?

[02:03] Sofia: Redwood doesn't replace your search stack — we integrate. you can do hybrid by combining your BM25 candidate sets with embeddings from redwood, then call our rerank endpoints to score and re-order. some customers push hybrid scoring into their index (e.g., OpenSearch) and then call redwood for final model-based rerank.
[02:18] Daniel: latency budget — can you give ballpark p95 numbers for hosted vs dedicated for a rerank of top 100 with a small transformer reranker?

[02:26] Ethan: ballpark: hosted API on shared capacity might give p95 ~200-500ms depending on batching and throughput. dedicated with pinned GPUs and optimized kernels can be 60-200ms p95. private/on-prem could be similar to dedicated if hardware is comparable. these are rough and we recommend benchmarks for your workload.
[02:40] Priya: understood. what about cost tradeoffs? moving to lower-dim embeddings reduces vector store size a lot but may hurt quality. any tooling to compare?

[02:48] Sofia: yes — redwood optimize has a recommendation engine: it suggests quantization, dimensionality experiments, and gives estimated token/embedding costs. we can run an eval with a sample of your queries to provide quality/cost tradeoff curves.
[02:58] Priya: great — we have eval sets for relevancy tests (2k queries) that we could share.
[03:03] Ethan: perfect. we can run A/B between 1536 and 768 embeddings and report recall/precision + cost. also can test hybrid recall when combining BM25 + vector rerank.
[03:12] Maya: security questions — for hosted, does redwood encrypt embeddings at rest? where are they stored?

[03:18] Sofia: hosted stores embeddings in our managed stores — encrypted at rest and in transit; we support customer-managed keys via KMS for enterprise plans, and audit logs. for strict requirements we'd recommend Dedicated with VPC private networking or Private deployment where your data never leaves your VPC.
[03:33] Daniel: do you have SOC2 and ISO certifications?
[03:36] Sofia: yes we are SOC2 Type II compliant, and we have docs we can share — i'll upload the security pack. we also support SSO/SAML and fine-grained RBAC in the console.
[03:44] Priya: onboarding — if we do a POC, what is the typical timeline?

[03:47] Ethan: typical POC is 2-6 weeks: week 1 onboarding + sample ingest, weeks 2-4 run benchmarks and quality evals, final weeks for tuning and recommendations. for dedicated/private add provisioning lead time (2-4 weeks for capacity in many regions).
[03:58] Ali (Product): for multi-region, is cross-region replication supported for indices?

[04:03] Ethan: we offer routing policies and can replicate model artifacts; for indices we integrate with your vector DB's replication or with dedicated setups we can set up multi-region pools. specifics depend on whether you're using our managed index or external store.
[04:14] Priya: can redwood run the reranker model for us or do we bring our own reranker?

[04:18] Sofia: both — we have pretrained rerankers and also support bringing your model (container or weights) to dedicated/private. we support function-calling style APIs and structured outputs if you want richer signals.
[04:27] Daniel: any rough numbers for disk footprint — 50M docs at 1536 dims with float32 is large. if we quantize to int8 or use IVF+PQ, what savings?

[04:36] Ethan: float32 is 6 GB per million vectors at 1536 dims roughly (ballpark) so 50M -> ~300GB raw; PQ/int8 can reduce 4-16x depending on settings; PQ + IVF reduces memory and speeds up search but affects recall. we can run indexed settings during a POC.
[04:49] Priya: regarding freshness: our index updates are frequent — ingest spikes nightly. do you support incremental updates without heavy reindex?

[04:55] Ethan: yes typical vector stores support incremental upserts; our recommended tight integration patterns minimize full reindexes. for big schema changes you may need reindexing but day-to-day adds are incremental.
[05:04] Maya: SLA and incident response — for dedicated customers do you offer SLOs?
[05:08] Sofia: yes Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and defined latency targets; Private deployments have support SLAs by contract. we also ship tracing hooks and per-route dashboards for debugging.
[05:17] Priya: who would own the POC? internal SRE or redwood SE?
[05:21] Ethan: redwood SE will run the benchmark and work with your SRE/ML engineer. typical attachments: benchmark spreadsheet, security pack, and a 2-week runbook.
[05:28] Daniel: ok can we talk about measurement — how will you measure recall/latency/cost?

[05:32] Ethan: we'll run the sample workload across 24-72 hours: measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput, embedding time, and cost-per-query. for quality we run your eval queries and compute nDCG/MRR and provide logs for analysis.
[05:43] Priya: any gotchas for our stack — we use milvus + postgres metadata + k8s, and sometimes we see GC/ooms with large batches.

[05:50] Ethan: that's common. we recommend continuous batching tuning and KV-cache management on the reranker side. dedicated nodes with pinned GPUs help reduce OOMs. also careful shard sizing for milvus.

[05:59] Sofia: just to capture next steps quickly — we'll send you a security pack, an example benchmark plan, and a pricing estimate for hosted vs dedicated. we'll also propose a POC scope. does that align?
[06:08] Priya: yes. we'd like the A/B for 1536 vs 768 and a hybrid BM25+vector config. timeframe: want POC within next 3 weeks.
[06:15] Daniel: and region note — EU data must stay in eu-west; can you support that?
[06:19] Sofia: yes EU-only hosting available for hosted enterprise, dedicated in eu-west, and private in your VPC. we'll note that for the quote.
[06:25] Ali: what about tokenization/embedding drift — do you offer monitoring for regressions after model swaps?
[06:30] Ethan: yes Redwood Optimize has quality monitoring tied to prompt sets/evals; it can alert on regressions and recommend rollback.
[06:35] Priya: would you be able to share previous similar POC results?
[06:38] Sofia: we have anonymized benchmark case studies — we'll attach a couple that are relevant (SaaS search and customer support rerankers).
[06:44] Maya: final question — do you provide a local runner or docker image for Private deployments?
[06:48] Ethan: yes we have an on-prem package with an air-gapped option; installation is via helm chart or container images and we provide operator docs.
[06:55] Sofia: ok i'll summarize and capture action items — thanks all for the time.
